Title: Deepfake video deception detection using visual attention-based method
Authors: K. Lal, S. Shiwani, G. C. Gandhi
Research Problem: Detecting subtle facial deepfake manipulations across compressed video sequences by focusing attention on artifact-rich spatial regions.
Method / Architecture: ResNeXt-50 (32x4d) + Soft Spatial Attention + Bidirectional LSTM (2048 hidden) + FC Binary Classifier
Evaluation Metrics: Accuracy, ROC-AUC, Precision, Recall, F1, EER
Limitations: High computational cost (batch 32, ~101 epochs); performance drops on severe compression; cross-dataset evaluation protocol lacks group stratification details.
Relevance to DeepGuard: Primary reference methodology reproduced by DeepGuard v1-baseline; direct architectural benchmark.
Verification / Source Notes: Verified via Nature Scientific Reports publisher portal & DOI 10.1038/s41598-025-23920-0. Local PDF present in Base_Papers/.

Title: FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images
Authors: A. Rössler, D. Cozzolino, L. Verdoliva, C. Riess, J. Thies, M. Nießner
Journal / Conference: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV 2019), pp. 1-11
Research Problem: Establishing large-scale facial forgery benchmarks with multiple compression tiers (Raw, C23, C40) and 4 forgery methods.
Reported Results: Xception C23: Acc 95.73%; Raw: Acc 99.26%; C40: Acc 81.00%
Limitations: Severe detection drop on C40 heavy compression; detectors overfit to specific forgery algorithms.
Relevance to DeepGuard: Ground-truth benchmark dataset provider (FF++ C23) and foundational evaluation protocol for DeepGuard.

Title: Thinking in Frequency: Face Forgery Detection by Mining Frequency-Aware Clues
Authors: Y. Qian, G. Yin, L. Sheng, Z. Chen, J. Shao
Journal / Conference: European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV 2020), pp. 86–103
Research Problem: Overcoming spatial blurring in compressed deepfakes by extracting artifact clues from the frequency domain.
Method / Architecture: Frequency-aware Decomposition (FAD) + Local Frequency Statistics (LFS) + Dual-stream Xception
Reported Results: FF++ C23: Acc 99.04%, AUC 0.992; Cross Celeb-DF: AUC 0.768
Limitations: Sensitivity to post-processing frequency perturbations (e.g. anti-aliasing filtering).
Relevance to DeepGuard: Motivates DeepGuard's high-frequency residual branch (M13.3) and DCT dual-stream cross-attention (M18).
Verification / Source Notes: Verified via Springer ECCV proceedings & DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-58610-2_6. Local PDF present.

Title: Spatial-Phase Shallow Learning: Rethinking Face Forgery Detection in Frequency Domain
Authors: H. Liu, X. Li, W. Zhou, Y. Chen, Y. He, H. Xue, W. Zhang, N. Yu
Journal / Conference: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2021), pp. 772–781
Research Problem: Detecting forged faces that blend seamlessly in spatial RGB by capturing phase spectrum anomalies.
Method / Architecture: Spatial-Phase Shallow Learning (SPSL) combining spatial RGB and phase spectrum via FFT into a shallow CNN
Reported Results: FF++ C23: Acc 91.50%, AUC 0.953; Celeb-DF cross AUC 0.778
Limitations: Requires precise face alignment; phase representations are sensitive to lossy video resizing.
Relevance to DeepGuard: Directly informs DeepGuard's Phase C forensic factor analysis (Mahalanobis facial manifold overlap).
Verification / Source Notes: Verified via IEEE CVPR proceedings & CVF Open Access. Local PDF present.

Title: Deepfake video detection: YOLO-Face and convolutional LSTM based approach
Authors: A. Ismail, M. Elpeltagy, M. S. Zaki, K. A. ElDahshan
Research Problem: Real-time facial detection and temporal artifact tracking in compressed streaming video.

Authors: D. Wodajo, H. Mareen, P. Lambert

Title: Face X-ray for More General Face Forgery Detection
Authors: L. Li, J. Bao, T. Zhang, H. Yang, D. Chen, F. Fang, B. Guo
Journal / Conference: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2020), pp. 5001-5010
Research Problem: Detecting arbitrary unseen face manipulations without training on specific manipulation algorithms.
Method / Architecture: HRNet / ResNet-50 trained on synthetic blending boundary prediction (Face X-ray)
Reported Results: FF++ C23: AUC 0.9852; Celeb-DF cross AUC: 0.7476
Limitations: Cannot detect entire synthetic face generation (e.g. StyleGAN) or manipulations without blending seams.
Relevance to DeepGuard: Explains why boundary detectors struggle on Face2Face and NeuralTextures; guides DeepGuard M13 invariant design.

Title: MesoNet: a Compact Facial Video Forgery Detection Network
Authors: D. Afchar, V. Nozick, J. Yamagishi, I. Echizen
Journal / Conference: IEEE International Workshop on Information Forensics and Security (WIFS 2018), pp. 1-7
Research Problem: Microscopic facial artifact detection using compact, lightweight deep convolutional networks.
Dataset(s): Proprietary Deepfake and Face2Face datasets, early FF++

Limitations: Severe vulnerability to lossy video compression; failure on modern GAN-generated textures.
Relevance to DeepGuard: Historical baseline demonstrating the necessity of temporal modeling and attention mechanisms.

Title: Fake-checker: A fusion of texture and frequency features for deepfake video detection
Authors: N. U. Huda, A. Javed, K. Masood, A. Irtaza

Title: Exposing deepfake using fusion of spatial and temporal features
Authors: A. Megahed, Q. Han, S. Fadl
Research Problem: Improving temporal consistency tracking by fusing spatial frame features with recurrent temporal descriptors.

Relevance to DeepGuard: Serves as an external benchmark for DeepGuard's temporal fusion and calibration experiments.

Title: Exposing DeepFake Videos By Detecting Eye Blinking
Authors: Y. Li, M.-C. Chang, S. Lyu
